title: Statement Regarding the Publication of Reference Rates on Friday, April 3, 2026

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: The New York Fed announced that SOFR, TGCR, BGCR, and SOFR Averages/Index will not be published on Friday, April 3, 2026 due to the overlap of Good Friday and the March Employment Situation report release. While SIFMA did not recommend a full market closure, repo market participants broadly expect to treat the date as a holiday, with cleared Treasury repo settlement unavailable.
key_points: SOFR, TGCR, BGCR, and SOFR Averages/Index will not publish on April 3, 2026
EFFR and OBFR will publish on April 3, 2026 as they follow the New York Fed's holiday schedule
Settlement of cleared Treasury repo is not scheduled to be available on April 3
This eliminates two of the three market segments used to calculate Treasury repo reference rates
On April 6, TGCR, BGCR, and SOFR will resume publication reflecting Thursday April 2 settlements maturing Monday April 6
The SOFR Averages and Index published April 6 will have a value date of April 6
why_it_matters: This operating policy notice documents a market infrastructure scenario where key overnight reference rates (SOFR, TGCR, BGCR) will be unavailable for one business day due to the overlap of Good Friday and the March Employment Situation report release. Participants relying on SOFR for derivatives pricing, collateral management, or overnight fund valuations need to account for this publication gap. The gap affects the SOFR Averages and Index calculations, which require consistent underlying rate data.
market_structure_context: The notice highlights critical market plumbing dependencies: cleared Treasury repo settlement is essential for calculating TGCR and BGCR, and without it, two of three Treasury repo market segments used to compute SOFR are unavailable. This demonstrates how interconnected market infrastructure is with reference rate integrity and why any disruption to repo settlement cascades into reference rate publication.

issues_found: The phrase 'unusual overlap' in why_it_matters is an editorial characterization not present in the source text. The source simply states the factual overlap without labeling it as unusual.

notes: Source is a straightforward New York Fed operating policy statement from March 12, 2026, announcing reference rate publication arrangements for an upcoming holiday/employment report overlap. Content is factual, clearly authored, and from a trusted domain. The 45-day gap between publication date and TODAY (2026-04-26) does not affect relevance as this is procedural/market plumbing information rather than time-sensitive commentary. The overlap with March Employment Situation release date is a notable market structure consideration.
